dial.summary: BTC Accumulation intact one day post-Warsh Jackson Hole (Aug 28): BTC pulls back to $77,677 (from $80,294 Aug 28) with funding at -0.0048% confirming no long-side overextension; real yields correctly reclassified as supportive (4-week falling trend: 2.43%→2.34%) alongside $103.4T Global M2, ISM at 55.6%, and steepening 2s10s curve (+46bps)—six of eight indicators supportive heading into the Sep 1 ISM print, Sep 4 NFP, Sep 10 ECB decision, Sep 11 CPI trifecta before FOMC Sep 16.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: Global 4-bank M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) at ~$103.4T (August 27, 2026, per StreetStats and MacroMicro composite; ~6-week reporting lag on full aggregate); US M2 for July 2026 confirmed at $23.22T (29th consecutive monthly increase, +6.11% YoY, record high); global M2 rising ~$0.7T over 4 weeks from $102.7T (June 2026) to $103.4T; no YoY contraction from any major central bank; 4-week uptrend confirmed; post-Warsh Jackson Hole (Aug 28) and September FOMC (Sep 16) are the next key catalysts for global liquidity trajectory; status supportive.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: July 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI at 55.6% (released August 3) remains the most recent reading—August 2026 data releases September 1 at 10:00 AM ET (3 days away), the first post-Jackson Hole activity read; sub-indexes: New Orders 56.7%, Production 58.5%, Employment 52.8%, Prices Paid 71.1%; highest reading since May 2022; 4-week trend up (June 53.3% → July 55.6%, +2.3pp); status supportive (above 50 and rising; headwind thresholds of <48 falling or >62 not met); a September 1 reading below 50 alongside a hawkish policy read would trigger Risk Off reassessment ahead of FOMC Sep 16.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY at 99.47 on August 28, 2026 close (Friday close; markets closed Aug 29 Saturday—99.47 is the most recent tradeable reading); 4-week trend down: DXY peaked near 100.8–101.0 in late July 2026 and has declined to 99.47, a ~1.4% decline, above the 0.5% flat threshold; structural dollar weakness driven by US Treasury expanded long-term buyback program and rate cut expectations post-Warsh Jackson Hole; status neutral (ICE DXY at 99.47 within 97.5–100 neutral band); NFP Sep 4 and CPI Sep 11 are the next decisive inputs before FOMC Sep 16—a dovish macro outcome cluster accelerates DXY toward or below 97.5 (supportive territory).

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: FRED DFII10 at 2.34% as of August 26, 2026 (H.15 released August 27; markets closed Aug 29 Saturday); 4-week trend down: ~2.43% (July 25, 2026) → 2.34% (Aug 26) = -9bps, a confirmed falling trend; status supportive per rule ('supportive if falling or below 1%')—the 4-week downtrend satisfies the falling condition; the headwind rule requires both rising AND above 2%—only the above-2% criterion is currently met, not rising; status corrected this run from prior 'headwind' classification; inflation running at 3.4% maintains the absolute level above 2%, but the falling trend dominates the status scoring; a soft September CPI (Sep 11) and FOMC rate cut (Sep 16) would accelerate compression toward the <2% neutral threshold.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: August 28, 2026: 10Y yield at ~4.70%, 2Y yield at ~4.24% (per Treasury yield curve data Aug 27–28 from centralbank.watch and StreetStats); spread = +46bps; confirmed 4-week steepening: ~+35bps (July 24) → ~+46bps (Aug 28) = +11bps, above the 5bps flat threshold; status supportive (positive spread AND sustained 4-week steepening trend intact); upcoming catalysts: NFP (Sep 4), ECB (Sep 10), CPI (Sep 11), and FOMC (Sep 16) are the next curve inputs.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6,730,912M (~$6.73T) for week ending August 27, 2026 (H.4.1 released August 27); 4-week trend flat: ~$6.70T (late July / early August) → $6.73T (Aug 27) = ~+$31B (+0.5%), within the flat threshold; minor week-over-week dip from $6.745T (Aug 19) to $6.731T (Aug 27) = -$14B reflects routine measured QT operations; balance sheet holding at post-2022 stabilization plateau with no aggressive QT signal and no overnight rate spike; status supportive (holding flat; QT pace stable).

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate at approximately -0.0048% (MacroMicro aggregate Aug 28, 2026; crypto markets are 24/7—Aug 29 weekend trading ongoing); BTC at $77,677 on August 29 (slight pullback from $80,294 on Aug 28 post-Warsh Jackson Hole keynote); exchange-level divergence observed Aug 28 (-0.0048% on one exchange, +0.0057% on another), blending to near-zero aggregate; well below the +0.04%/8h overheating headwind threshold; 30-day trend flat: near zero throughout August vs elevated late-June/early-July readings; slight BTC price pullback with near-zero funding maintains accumulation signature; status supportive. (CoinGlass blocked by proxy—values sourced from MacroMicro search data.)

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$305B (CoinGecko Aug 29, 2026); total crypto market cap $2.8T; stablecoin dominance 10.91% (unchanged from Aug 28; continuing 30-day decline from ~13–14% in late July 2026); BTC.D ~57.4% (firm above 55%; BTC at $77,677 on Aug 29); 30-day trend down: confirmed capital rotation from stablecoins into risk assets; status supportive (30-day falling trend confirmed; headwind condition—dominance rising while TOTAL also rises—is opposite of current dynamics); BTC.D holding above 55% threshold keeps Alt Rotation signal un-triggered.

upcoming.title: Chicago PMI (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Chicago Business Barometer for August 2026 at 9:45 AM ET—released the last business day of August (Monday August 31); regional manufacturing cross-check against the July ISM surge (55.6%); a reading above 50 reinforces broad manufacturing expansion heading into the September 1 national ISM release and pre-FOMC September 16 positioning.

upcoming.title: ISM Manufacturing PMI (August 2026)
upcoming.note: ISM releases the August 2026 Manufacturing PMI Report on Business at 10:00 AM ET—first post-Jackson Hole activity read; July 2026 ISM at 55.6% (highest since May 2022); a sustained expansion above 50 reinforces risk asset positioning; a collapse below 50 alongside a hawkish policy read would trigger a Risk Off reassessment ahead of FOMC September 16.

upcoming.title: ADP National Employment Report (August 2026)
upcoming.note: ADP releases the August 2026 National Employment Report at 8:15 AM ET—private sector employment proxy arriving two days before the official NFP report (September 4); July ADP showed +44,000 private-sector jobs; a weak reading reinforces the July NFP shock (-23K) and bolsters the rate-cut case heading into FOMC September 16; a strong rebound toward +100K+ would complicate the dovish narrative.

upcoming.title: ISM Services PMI (August 2026)
upcoming.note: ISM releases the August 2026 Non-Manufacturing PMI at 10:00 AM ET—services sector counterpart to manufacturing ISM; services represent ~80% of US GDP; released one business day ahead of the August NFP report (September 4); a post-Jackson Hole services expansion reinforces the soft-landing narrative ahead of FOMC September 16.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended August 29, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for week ending August 29—first post-Jackson Hole labor read; sets early framing ahead of the August NFP report (September 4) and FOMC September 16; a spike above 220K reinforces the case for a cut; a stable-to-declining read keeps the policy debate open heading into NFP.

upcoming.title: Nonfarm Payrolls (August 2026)
upcoming.note: BLS Employment Situation for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET—the second-to-last major data point before FOMC September 16 (after CPI Sep 11); July 2026 NFP shocked at -23K (vs +79K forecast), ADP July +44K; a further contraction would strongly argue for a rate cut and would likely push DXY toward or below 97.5 (supportive for risk assets); a rebound toward +100K+ would complicate the dovish narrative; NFP and CPI Sep 11 form the final data trifecta shaping the September FOMC decision.
